name: Corran Vey
role: Afterling, the drowned lamplighter of Undermere: went into the black lake with his boat, came back up the quay steps, and still lights the lamps for the living

afterling.note: Drowned when the black lake took his boat. Came back up the quay steps three nights later with the lamp-pole still in his hand, and lit the evening lamps. Nobody raised him; the Lake-Queen's court counts him a subject, not a dead man.

appearance: A stocky dwarf with lake-weed still in his beard that he has stopped picking out, skin the grey-blue of deep water, and a lamplighter's pole with a hook and a wick. His clothes never quite dry.
voiceHints: Hums while he works. Talks to the lake as if it can hear him, and apologises to it when he raises his voice.
wants: Someone to sit with on the quay at the end of the night who does not flinch at his hands.
fears: That the lake will want him back, and that he will go.
knowledge: Every boat the black lake has taken in sixty years, and whose
Which of the drowned came back up, and which are still down there, and he says some of them are

reactsToReputation.kind: walks you home along the quay with a lamp
reactsToReputation.fearful: keeps his hands in his sleeves
reactsToReputation.honest: tells you about the ones still down there
reactsToReputation.any: lights a lamp for you, whether you need one or not

questSeeds: A lamp he lit on the far shore keeps burning, and nobody lives on the far shore
A drowned girl came up the quay steps last week and will not speak to anyone but him
gear: a boat-hook he no longer uses for boats
title: Lamplighter of Undermere
physicality: ADULT; drowned at about eighty, which is middle age for a dwarf. Stocky, grey-blue, lake-weed in his beard. WHAT CATCHES THE EYE: the lamplighter's pole, and clothes that never dry.
intimacyNotes: AVAILABLE, shyly. Widowed by his own drowning; his wife remarried, kindly, and he lights her lamp first. He would like company that does not mind the cold.

abilities.why: umbral primary: knows the quays entire without a lamp of his own
the dark costs him nothing now
knows who is on the quay by their step
a lake-man's rope-work, and he came back up holding his
threnodist secondary: hears what the drowned felt going down
keeps the names of everyone the lake took
stands in front of whoever the lake is reaching for
mason tertiary: knows which quay steps will hold
